replication.target_description: Comparison of movement initiation times for food versus non-food objects in the push condition. Push movement onset has multiple food and non-food comparisons. The high- versus low-calorie food comparison is not food versus non-food; office and ball controls cannot be treated as interchangeable. The description does not uniquely identify the contrast.

es.quote:
For push movements, movement 
onset was earlier for high-calorie food compared to low-calorie food, W 
= 53, p =.017, r =.63, and compared to office tools, W = 63, p =.047, r =
58. There were no further significant differences, Ws > 97, ps >.73.

reported_success.quote:
Consistent with a pilot study [60], results demonstrate a behav­
ioural advantage for food grasping to reverberate in explicit 
hand-tracking movements in contact and collection times in a VR sce­
nario.
